subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define execution anti-drift as a core durable run-state contract, and which artifact, timer, persistence, feature-flag, and post-green semantics should it enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested fix chooses public runtime semantics, persisted state ownership, operator-visible escalation behavior, and config/default shape across core agent execution.

options.title: Design core contract first
options.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

options.title: Fold into existing lifecycle surfaces
options.body: Extend current loop detection, heartbeat response, task status, subagent lifecycle, and cron watchdog paths without creating a parallel state source.

options.title: Narrow to a smaller reproducible gap
options.body: Keep this umbrella open only for the missing status-artifact contract and move broader silence or delivery-confirmation policy to the existing related issues.

recommendation.title: Design core contract first
recommendation.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest adjacent history across loop detection, diagnostic liveness thresholds, and agent lifecycle behavior, making him the best available routing owner for the product-contract choice.
